text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AutoPager triggered for inference-gateway prod (eu-west1) — sustained 5xx spike. 5m error rate jumped from ~2% to 9%. PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-77821 (sev2). Auto-escalation chain started. Please ack.

jordan_oncall: acked. I'm on it. grabbing charts + runbook. Can someone drop the relevant grafana link?

ana_sre: grafana -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ig/egress-5xx?orgId=1&from=now-15m to now. Seeing a sharp ingress 502/503 spike hitting the edge LB pools in eu-west1 only. Host 10.12.5.* showing increased backend timeouts.

mike_runtime: tagging in runtime. no new model rollouts in prod in last 30m. But we had a small autoscale event in eu-west1 ~12m ago. Could be conn saturation. Suggest: (1) disable canary route slice, (2) evict long-lived connections, (3) scale up dedicated pool if needed.

liz_support: customer-impact check: Top affected orgs by errors: AcmeCorp (20k requests, 14% errors), BetaHealth (6k requests, 11% errors). Support escalation in progress. ETA for customer DM?

jordan_oncall: quick checklist: - Is this a routing/LB problem or backend kvcache stall? I'm going to `curl` the health endpoints on a few gateways.

jordan_oncall: ```bash
curl -sS -D - https://ingress-eu-west1.redwood.prod/healthz | head -n 20
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# x-service: inference-gateway
# up: 1
```

mike_runtime: health looks OK on most pods. I'm seeing a pattern of `upstream prematurely closed connection` in the ingress logs. Log snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T02:13:17Z] ingress-nginx: 10.12.5.21:502 "POST /v1/generate" 502 312 "upstream prematurely closed connection" "req_id=abcd-1234"
[2026-03-15T02:13:22Z] ingress-nginx: 10.12.5.57:504 "POST /v1/chat" 504 198 "timeout waiting for response" "req_id=efgh-5678"
```

ana_sre: LB health checks show spike in 5xx at L7 with 502/504 codes; backend pods show memory usage >80% and occasional OOMKill on one replica. Could be pressure on the runtime (KV cache thrash).

maya_eng: I'm rolling an immediate scaledown of the canary slice -> set `slice.weight: 0` for routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat in eu-west1. Also starting a targeted restart of the 3 pods showing high memory.

jordan_oncall: good. I'm enabling a temporary traffic reroute to us-west1 for non-EU customers (policy: route by geo + customer-tier). That should mitigate impact for non-eu tenants. :white_check_mark:

liz_support: Customer comms: DM draft for AcmeCorp and BetaHealth: "We've detected elevated 5xx in eu-west1 impacting some inference requests. We've routed traffic and are mitigating; monitoring actively. Expect reduced errors within 10-20m. Will follow up with root cause and timeline." Approve?

ana_sre: approve. Also open an incident note: possible root causes: connection saturation at ingress -> backend runtime memory pressure -> kvcache eviction -> timeouts. Will capture heap/dumps if OOM recurs.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: if incident is not acknowledged by a senior SRE within 10m, auto-escalation to oncall-sre-lead will fire. Current ack chain contains 2 acks.

mike_runtime: I launched 4 additional runtime replicas in eu-west1 and bumped pool capacity. Monitoring backend 95th pct response time. Also temporarily disabled large-response streaming on the busiest route to reduce memory spike.

jordan_oncall: seeing error-rate dip to ~4% after restarts and reroute. Still above baseline but trending down. Keeping pages open until stable <1.5% for 30m.

maya_eng: restarted one machine that had repeated OOMs; collecting `/var/log/runtime/oom.txt` and uploading to the incident folder.

liz_support: customer update sent to AcmeCorp + BetaHealth. Both ack receipt and asked for ongoing updates. No P1 customer SLA breaches reported yet but watch for rate-dependent features.

ana_sre: adding mitigation summary to the incident: actions taken: scaled runtime + restarted offending pods + disabled canary slice + geo reroute for non-EU + throttled streaming routes. Next steps: root cause postmortem, memory profiling, KV cache tuning.

jordan_oncall: thanks team. If error rate stays under 2% for 35m we'll close. Leaving this thread open for another 45m for monitoring handoff. :coffee:
